beats: Hook (line_qc_ft_patch_new_hole, then the cover): every error check is built from CNOT gates, and a CNOT can turn one error into two; a code that fixes one error per block now faces two. How can correction work when the corrector is noisy too? The question was a student's (Q24-09 23:29): paraphrase it in a caption, clip only her answer (Q24-09 23:50-24:30). Same cast as QC08-05: the keeper and the imp; closes the error-correction block.

Compute on encoded data: classical schemes decode, compute and encode again; a fault-tolerant machine stays encoded the whole time and decodes only at the end, if at all (Q25-11 68:11-69:01) (line_qc_ft_glovebox: work through the gloves, never open the box). Her word for it, bootstrapping (clip Q24-13 01:58-02:25): the code is the core and everything is built on it while it runs (line_qc_ft_ship_at_sea: new planks fitted at sea, no dry dock).

A CNOT spreads errors (69:08-71:24): an X error on the control is copied forward to the target; a Z error on the target is copied backward to the control (line_qc_ft_skaters_slip: the leader slips and pulls the follower down; the Z-backward rule stays a code-drawn circuit, not the skaters). Clip 70:56-71:24 "error propagation will kill you".

Inside one block, spreading is a cascade: one fault becomes several errors in the same block, more than a one-error code can fix (line_qc_ft_domino_block; reuse line_qc_cnot_three_legged from QC05-04 for "two-qubit gates tie qubits together").

Transversal gates (71:31-72:52, clip 71:31-72:26): a logical CNOT between two seven-qubit Steane blocks made of seven CNOTs, gate i touching only qubit i of each block; a single fault reaches at most one qubit per block, which each block can fix (line_qc_ft_dance_pairs). Tape Q25-11 s27 and s28 (crop the footer).

Logical X and Z (72:54-75:34): commute with every check, are not checks, and anticommute with each other; the silent error of QC08-05, done on purpose, is a logical gate (line_qc_ft_flip_all_on_purpose, the mirror of line_qc_catch_all_three_flipped).

Not every gate can be transversal (72:26-72:52): no code has a universal transversal gate set (Eastin-Knill 2009); the T gate is the hard one, made with magic states (reuse line_qc_tgate_distillery from QC05-03). Below the threshold, more encoding wins (callback QC01-03: reuse line_qc_analog_bail_boats or line_qc_analog_toll_tunnel). Still a research field.
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_08; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the keeper hammers a patch onto a rowboat and the nail splits a new leak; the imp holds a bucket at the stern.
